title: Fallback interop gap analysis and compatibility catalog refactor
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
We need a focused gap analysis and a pragmatic refactor of the fallback compatibility catalog used by smart routing. The existing matrix primarily lists pass/fail flags for tokenizer and KV cache compatibility, but it is brittle, hard to maintain, and lacks programmatic signals for runtime routing. This ticket scopes an engineering-first remediation: introduce a compatibility scoring model, add automation to detect regressions across tokenizers/context lengths/tooling hooks, and refactor the catalog data model so downstream routers and rollout services can consume stable signals.

Goals:
- Produce a prioritized gap list of variant pairs that currently fail interoperability tests across tokenizer, KV cache, and tool-calling interfaces.
- Design and implement a compact compatibility schema (score + categorical flags + last-verified timestamp + verification-run-id) to replace the current ad-hoc matrix.
- Wire an automated verification pipeline that runs on candidate commits and nightly sweeps, emits signals to routing layer and the Console (badges + telemetry).
- Create migration tooling to backfill the new catalog and mark safe fallbacks for canary routing rules.

Success metrics:
- Reduce manual compatibility issues filed by SE/PM teams against fallback routing by 70% in the first quarter after rollout.
- Every routing decision can read a deterministic compatibility score for a fallback candidate within 200ms.
- Nightly sweep reduces unknown/untested pairs count by 90% vs current baseline.

Non-goals:
- Full tokenizer reimplementation or deep fixes to each model; this ticket focuses on detection, metadata, and operational controls.

Approach & deliverables:
1) Audit phase (week 1): run targeted test matrix across top-10 high-traffic variants (by invocation volume) for tokenizer parity, KV-cache recovery, and tool-call payload compatibility. Produce CSV of failures and per-pair reproduction snippets.
2) Schema design (week 2): define compact JSON record per pair: {"pair_key","score","flags","last_verified","verifier_run_id","notes"} and API contract for the router to query.
3) Compatibility scoring (week 2): lightweight scoring function combining unit test pass-rate, tokenization divergence ratio on corpus, and tooling-call handshake success.
4) Backfill & migration (week 3): script to convert current matrix to new schema, mark uncertainty thresholds, and tag high-risk fallbacks for manual review.
5) Automation & CI (week 4): integrate verification harness into PR checks for model onboarding and a nightly job that emits metrics to Observability (Console).
6) Rollout (week 5): flip router consumer to trust score when available; fallback to flag-based behavior while monitoring. 1-week canary in region us-east1 only before global rollout.

Instrumentation & observability:
- New metrics: compatibility_pairs_tested, compatibility_score_distribution, fallback_route_rejections, router_fallback_latency_added.
- Console dashboard: compatibility heatmap, per-model badge (green/yellow/red), verification-run history.

Deliverables (artifacts):
- Confluence: gap analysis doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-860931+-+Compat+Gap+Analysis)
acceptance_criteria: Schema PR merged and documented in API reference
Nightly verification job created with >95% reliability in the first run window
Backfill completes without data loss and marks at least 90% of previous pairs as verified/unknown
Router integration reads compatibility score and uses it for fallback selection under canary policy
Console dashboard shows per-pair last_verified and score badges
steps: Run initial audit matrix on anbn-corpus and prod-proxy workload sample
Prototype scoring function and simulate router outcomes on historical traffic
Create migration script and dry-run on staging catalog snapshot
Add CI gate that rejects model onboarding PRs with score < 0.4 for default fallback eligibility
Deploy canary router change to us-east1 with traffic shadowing and monitoring alerts
